description:
This project is a Python workflow for building and evaluating three-dimensional seismic velocity models of the Earth's crust from earthquake recordings. It was developed for the Permian Basin of West Texas and southeastern New Mexico. The workflow supports travel-time tomography, an imaging method that uses the arrival times of seismic waves at many stations to infer subsurface wave speeds. It is built around LATTE (Los Alamos Travel-Time package based on the Eikonal Equation), an open-source tomography and earthquake relocation code. The research problem it addresses is practical: moving from raw earthquake catalogs to a trustworthy velocity model takes many error-prone, hand-made steps. This repository makes those steps scripted, configurable, and repeatable.

It has three connected pipelines, each controlled by simple configuration files:
Preprocessing: reads earthquake catalogs (QuakeML or HDF5 format), converts coordinates, and prepares the travel-time, station-geometry, and starting-model files that the LATTE inversion needs.
Post-processing: turns the LATTE inversion's binary outputs into open tables (CSV and HDF5) holding the updated velocity models, travel-time residuals, relocated earthquakes, ray paths, and ray-coverage measures.
Analysis: produces quality-control plots, statistics, and reports, including travel-time residuals, velocity differences, source relocations, and trade-off curves between data fit and model change.
The repository also includes resolution tests (checkerboard and spike tests) that show which parts of a model are well constrained, along with worked examples and documentation.

The workflow is designed to be reused. Seismologists can apply it to other induced-seismicity regions. Researchers can reproduce and check the Permian Basin results. Others can test new inversion settings, compare models, or use the analysis-ready tables to train machine-learning models and develop new studies. What makes it distinctive is that it covers the whole tomography process, from the earthquake catalog to the final diagnostics, in one open, documented package, and that it is tied to a real, densely monitored induced-seismicity region. It is mainly for earthquake seismologists, geophysicists, geotechnical and hazard engineers, and students.
